C08-M03-L04-F1.title: R2 vpn_spray_then_success: how the rule decides
C08-M03-L04-F1.caption: The minisiem sequence rule as the engine evaluates it: two event roles, an entity join, an order condition, a distinct-count grouping and a threshold.
C08-M03-L04-F1.alt: Top-to-bottom graph. Two blue inputs, VPN successes (s) and VPN failures (f), both feed an orange box Join on src_ip. It leads to a violet Time condition box (f.ts <= s.ts, no lower bound), then a violet Group per success box (COUNT DISTINCT f.user), then a violet decision box users_failed >= 5?. The yes branch leads to a dark Alert box: 203.0.113.66, 8 users failed, then gopal succeeded at 06:46:00Z. The no branch leads to a slate No alert box.
C08-M03-L04-F1.note: Add an upper bound to the time condition: with 10 minutes the rule fires, with 2 minutes it misses this spray.

C08-M03-L04-F2.title: The Banyan storyline on one UTC timeline
C08-M03-L04-F2.caption: Storyline events from four sources between 06:00 and 08:30 UTC; four rows belong to host WS-104, the VPN row to an account and address.
C08-M03-L04-F2.alt: Timeline with five rows from 06:00 to 08:30 UTC. Proxy download and upload (orange): ticks at 06:12 and 08:12. Sysmon WINWORD to PowerShell (red): one tick at 06:14. Proxy beacon every 5 minutes (red): 18 evenly spaced ticks from 06:17 to 07:42. Windows 4720, 4732, 1102 (violet): ticks at 07:02, 07:03 and 08:17. VPN spray and success for gopal (blue): a cluster of 8 failures at 06:42 and a success at 06:46. The first four rows are host WS-104; the VPN events carry no host.
C08-M03-L04-F2.note: Four rows share host WS-104 and can be joined; the VPN row overlaps in time but shares no entity with them.
